opportunity: `kuna decompile-all` and `kuna decompile` must produce the same C for the same binary, address and mode -- decompile-all was the weaker path, and it is the one decbench, the web front-end, decompile-project and every agent-facing whole-binary workflow use
test_name: kuna decompile vs kuna decompile-all, same --addr and --mode, over 13 real binaries x 4 modes (182 records) + the 4 vendored fmt_<arch> fixtures
change_kind: correctness-fix (surface parity) + mode-preset change (`formatstring` leaves AGGRESSIVE_OVERRIDES on the speed gate)
inspiration: IDA Pro 9.2 renders `void error(const char *a1)` where kuna decompile-all rendered `void error(unsigned long a0)` and kuna decompile rendered `void error(char *a0)` -- the same binary, the same address, the same mode
upstream_anchor: Ghidra FormatStringAnalyzer (DecompilerDependent) -- one analyzer, applied by whatever drives the decompiler, not by one front-end
upstream_fidelity: restores the analyzer's surface-independence; upstream has no notion of an analyzer that applies to one front-end only
root_cause: Two call sites for one pipeline. IfcDecompile wrapped decompile_func_full_with_override_dyn in the FormatStringAnalyzer half-B override/re-decompile loop and enabled readonlypropagate for its duration; project::decompile_targets called the drive directly. So `--option formatstring on` -- which `--mode aggressive` names, and `auto` selects for anything under 500 KiB -- was a silent no-op on decompile-all, decompile-project and the WASM front-end. The scoped readonlypropagate flip is the larger of the two effects: it constant-folds every read-only load, so on ARM Cortex-M (literal pools) it rewrites most of a function body, not just its printf call sites.
ruled_out: a --mode plumbing bug (both surfaces resolve the mode through the same decompile_all::mode_options_for_binary, and an explicit --option formatstring on was equally inert on decompile-all)
a load/analysis-tier difference (both surfaces inject `option listing on`; the divergent functions carried identical names, callee names and call graphs)
decompile-all never setting the option (analysis_formatstring IS true there; nothing read it)
the loop needing console state (it consumes only &Architecture and the first decompile's Funcdata)
the flow-extent bound (console re-drives with fd.get_size(), the loop with 0/unbounded) -- 0 residual differences in 182 records
function naming under --addr (function_display_name_across_scopes vs the canonical find_entry_at record) -- 0 name differences in 182 records

optimization_attempted_and_rejected.idea: decline an override whose format-derived types already equal the call's argument types, so the caller need not be decompiled twice
optimization_attempted_and_rejected.output_effect: changed emitted C on 12 of 15,990 functions (7 of 33 cases) -- it breaks the parity this PR exists for
optimization_attempted_and_rejected.verdict: REVERTED: buys ~nothing (the redundant overrides sit in the same functions as real ones, so the caller re-decompiles anyway) and is not output-preserving
optimization_attempted_and_rejected.why_the_cost_is_large_anyway: only 15%/5%/10% of functions re-decompile on crontab/psktool/gzip; they carry most of the decompile time because a printf-heavy function is a big function

follow_ups: formatstring: make the second decompile cheap (100% of the measured cost). The naive redundant-override skip was built and rejected -- see speed.optimization_attempted_and_rejected. This is the precondition for putting the option back into AGGRESSIVE_OVERRIDES, which is where the decbench type_match win lives

SEPARATE ROOT CAUSE, filed in the PR body: kuna cannot LOAD an unstripped C++ binary containing an anonymous namespace. strip_bracket_groups (kuna-analysis analyzers/demangle/mod.rs) deletes `(anonymous namespace)` whole, leaving an empty `::` component, and Database::find_create_scope_from_symbol_name rejects it with "Non-global scope has empty name" -- aborting `load file` for the entire binary. Both surfaces fail identically (it is NOT a divergence). Reproduces on leveldb libleveldb.so.1.23.0 and leveldbutil; 8 of leveldbutil's FUNC symbols reduce to an empty component. Pre-existing (the demangler predates #262-#266); invisible until now because decbench scores the STRIPPED binaries.
the shared step is the natural home for any further per-function driver policy (the watchdog budget is still armed by the CLI on the architecture rather than passed in)

formatstring: a %c argument is typed uint1 where the C variadic promotion makes the parameter an int (sysvinit Write_Runlevel_Log); a format-derived width can narrow a recovered uLong (zlib test_sync). Both pre-exist on `kuna decompile`; they are the 10 type_match regressions in this PR's benchmark
